fairValue._comment: Revenue-based over five years, because Rocket Lab has never earned an operating profit and the exit margin is the whole question. Tax is set to zero for the horizon — there are years of losses to work through first, and taxing the terminal year would flatter nothing since we are valuing on the exit multiple anyway. Net debt is negative: they hold about $2.4B of cash and securities against almost no borrowing. It does NOT model the Iridium acquisition, which is the single biggest thing that would change every input.

verdict.callLine: Flawless revenue execution, no progress at all on profit, and a {iridiumCash|usd} cash bill about to land.

why: Start with what is genuinely excellent, because a lot of it is. Revenue grew {revGrowth|%0} to {rev|usd}, a record, and they have now landed at or above the top of their own guidance seven quarters in a row. That is rare. Backlog more than doubled. Gross margin is {gmPct|%}. They are about to fly a reusable medium-lift rocket. Nobody should mistake this for a bad company.

Now the thing that stopped me. Line up eight quarters of operating loss and it does not move: {opLossMin|usd} to {opLossMax|usd}, every single quarter, while revenue grew {revOverPeriod|%0} from {revFirst|usd} to {rev|usd}. Every extra dollar of sales has been spent. That is a choice, not a failure — but it means the profit everyone is waiting for keeps being deferred one more year.

And look where the growth is. Launch revenue — the rockets, the thing this company is named after — fell {launchChangeAbs|%0} year over year to {launchRev|usd}. All of the growth is Space Systems, the satellite and components business. That is a good business. It is also a manufacturing business trading on a rocket company's multiple.

Then the bill. They have agreed to pay Iridium shareholders $27.00 a share in cash. On Iridium's own share count that is about {iridiumCash|usd}. Rocket Lab holds {netCashPos|usd}. The cash they have promised is larger than the cash they have, which means borrowing, issuing shares, or both — on top of a share count that has already grown {shareGrowth|%0} in a year.

So: not yet. I want to own the company that flies Neutron and turns Space Systems into real profit. I do not want to pay {psAnnualised|x0} revenue for it the week before it writes a cheque it cannot yet cover.

notes.title: Rocket Lab reported Q2 after the close today, and the stock is down about ten percent in after-hours trading. Nothing is settled — the real verdict is tomorrow. But the filings are already public, so let's read them before the market decides. TARGET 22s.
notes.tape: Here is the two-year picture. It ran to a hundred and fifty dollars in May, then fell sixty-one percent to fifty-eight in July. It had clawed back to eighty-three by Friday. Then tonight's numbers. TARGET 24s.
notes.findings: Five things in tonight's filings that are not in tonight's headline. Every one comes from a document filed in the last few hours, or from the eight quarters before it. TARGET 26s.
notes.business: Two businesses. Launch Services flies Electron rockets. Space Systems builds satellites and the parts that go in them. Hold on to which is which, because the next slide is the whole episode. TARGET 22s.
notes.segments: This is the one. The release says record revenue, up sixty-two percent. Underneath, the rocket business shrank four point four percent. Every dollar of growth came from the satellite side. TARGET 30s.
notes.growth: And the growth itself is real and relentless. Seven quarters in a row they have landed at or above the top of their own guidance. That is genuinely hard to do. TARGET 24s.
notes.flatloss: Now put the loss underneath it. Revenue nearly doubled. The operating loss did not move — it has been between fifty-one and sixty million every single quarter for two years. Every extra dollar of sales was spent. TARGET 32s.
notes.opex: Here is where it went. Research and development up twenty-five percent, sales and admin up fifty percent. They are spending ahead of Neutron and ahead of the acquisitions. TARGET 24s.
notes.interest: And be careful with the improving net loss. Most of that improvement is interest on the two point four billion of cash they raised — not the business getting closer to profit. TARGET 26s.
notes.ebitda: Watch the adjusted number too. Adjusted losses of nine million against a real operating loss of fifty-eight million. Nineteen million of the difference is pay handed out in shares. TARGET 28s.
notes.gross: None of which means the product is bad. Gross margin is thirty-six percent and rising, and the launch side actually earns forty-three cents in the dollar now. The problem is below the gross line, not above it. TARGET 24s.
notes.backlog: Backlog is a record two point three six billion, more than double last year. One caveat, in the release's own footnote: the headline contract values include options the customer never has to exercise. TARGET 26s.
notes.iridium: And then this. They are buying Iridium — twenty-seven dollars a share in cash, plus stock. On Iridium's share count that cash is about two point nine billion. Rocket Lab has two point four. TARGET 32s.
notes.collar: The stock half has a collar. Between sixty-seven fifty and a hundred twelve fifty, Iridium holders get a fixed twenty-seven dollars of stock. Below sixty-seven fifty, the ratio locks. The stock is inside that band tonight, close to the bottom of it. TARGET 28s.
notes.insider: Nine hundred and twenty-four million of insider selling over the year. Not one share bought. Five hundred and fifty-seven million of it by the founder and chief executive. And fewer than four in ten of those filings mention a pre-set plan. TARGET 32s.
notes.valuation: So what are you paying. Annualise this quarter and it is about sixty times sales, for a company that has never earned an operating profit. TARGET 26s.
notes.peers: Against the defence primes it builds alongside — and against Iridium, the company it is buying — Rocket Lab is in a different universe on price. TARGET 24s.
notes.verdict: Six dimensions. The growth and the backlog are excellent. The profit path, the launch business and the price are not. TARGET 24s.
notes.twolists: What's working, and what I'd watch. TARGET 20s.
notes.fairvalue: My own arithmetic, and it has to be generous to get anywhere near tonight's price. TARGET 26s.
notes.call: Not yet. A company I want to own at a price I don't, the week before it writes a cheque it can't cover. Let's go to the chart. TARGET 30s.
